अभ्यास के पूर्व मनुष्य को आसनों का अभ्यास करना होता है, क्योंकि इससे श्वास की क्रियाओं में

अभ्यास इस युग के लिए नहीं है। इस युग में कोई भी योग में सिद्धि प्राप्त नहीं कर सकता। किन्तु
कुछ लोग आसनों का अभ्यास करते हैं, जो एक तरह से व्यायाम ही है। ऐसे शारीरिक व्यायाम से रक्त
संचार अच्छा हो सकता है और शरीर स्वस्थ रह सकता है, किन्तु यदि कोई इन्हीं व्यायामों तक अपने

सकता है और एक शरीर से दूसरे में या एक स्थान से दूसरे स्थान में ले जाया जा सकता है। दूसरे
शब्दों में, योगाभ्यास शरीर को स्वस्थ रखने के लिए नहीं होता। आध्यात्मिक अनुभूति की कोई भी
दिव्य क्रिया स्वतः ही शरीर को ठीक रखती है, क्योकि आत्मा से शरीर सदा स्वस्थ रहता है । ज्योंही
आत्मा शरीर को त्याग देता है, शरीर सड़ने लगता है । कोई भी आध्यात्मिक क्रिया बाह्य प्रयास के बिना
ही शरीर को स्वस्थ रखती है, किन्तु यदि कोई यह सोचता है कि योग की परिणति का अन्तिम लक्ष्य
शरीर की रक्षा है, तो वह भूल करता है। योग की वास्तविक सिद्धि तो आत्मा को उच्च पद पर पहुँचाना
है, अथवा आत्मा को भौतिक बन्धन से मुक्ति दिलाना है। कुछ योगी आत्मा को उच्चतर लोकों तक
ऊपर उठाने का प्रयास करते हैं, जहाँ का जीवन-स्तर इस लोक से भिन्न है ओर भौतिक सुविधाएँ,
जीवनकाल तथा आत्म-साक्षात्कार की अन्य सुविधाएँ अधिक हैं | कुछ योगी आत्मा को वैकुण्ठलोक
तक ले जाने का प्रयास करते हैं। भक्तियोग से तो आत्मा सीधे वैकुण्ठलोक जाता है जहाँ जीवन आनन्द
तथा ज्ञान से नित्य पूर्ण रहता है फलतः भक्तियोग को समस्त योग पद्धतियों में श्रेष्ठ समझा जाता है।

Meaning: The yogic action is the restraint of the air moving in the six chakras within the body. The air is taken from the abdomen
to the navel, from the navel to the heart, from the heart to the throat, from the throat to between both eyebrows, and finally from the middle of the eyebrows.
It is taken to the top part of the brain. This is the action of yoga practice ©. Before the actual yoga method,
a person has to practice asanas, because it helps in the functions of breathing
and can regulate the air going up and down. To attain the supreme perfected state of yoga, one has to practice this vast technique, but this
practice is not for this era. In this age, no one can attain perfection in yoga. But,
some people practice asanas, which is a kind of exercise.
Such physical exercise can improve blood circulation and keep the body healthy, but if someone limits themselves to these exercises,
they may not attain the highest state of perfection. Keshav-Shuti describes the action of yoga,
in which it is explained how the life force can be controlled according to one's will,
and how it can be transferred from one body to another or from one place to another. In other words, yoga practice is not meant to keep the body healthy. Any spiritual experience
A divine action automatically keeps the body healthy, because the body always remains healthy from the soul. As soon as
the soul leaves the body, the body starts to decay. Any spiritual practice, without external effort,
keeps the body healthy, but if someone thinks that the ultimate goal of yoga is
the protection of the body, then he is mistaken.
The real accomplishment of yoga is to elevate the soul to a higher position,
or to liberate the soul from material bondage. Some yogis try to elevate the soul to higher realms, where the standard of living is different from this realm, and physical facilities,
lifespan, and other facilities for self-realization are greater. Some yogis try to take the soul to Vaikuntha Loka. From Bhakti Yoga, the soul goes directly to Vaikuntha, where life is full of bliss and knowledge, and thus Bhakti Yoga is considered the best among all yoga practices.

When all the people were talking to each other, Daksha started seeing inauspicious signs ( ominous signs ) from all directions, from the earth, and from the sky. Meaning: In this verse, Daksha is called a Mahatma. The commentary on the word Mahatma has been done by various commentators

^ is stable-hearted. The meaning is that Daksha was so strong-hearted that his daughter was ready to give her life,
yet she did not tremble, she remained steadfast. Even after that, when he saw the various kinds of calamities caused by the demon Virat Shyam,
he was disturbed. In this regard, Vishwanath Chakraborty Thakur's comment is that even after being called a Mahatma, until the characteristics of a Mahatma are manifested in someone, one should consider them a wicked person. In the Bhagavad Gita (9.13), the word Mahatma has come for the pure devotee of God-- Mahatyansastu ma Partha daivi prakritimashritah.
A Mahatma always remains under the guidance of the inner power of God.
Therefore, how could a wicked man like Daksha be a Mahatma? In a Mahatma,
there should be all the virtues of the gods, therefore, how could a skilled person without these virtues be called a Mahatma?
He should be called a wicked person. Here, this word is used sarcastically.
